title: Pseudocode Workbook
subtitle: Independent practice for Cambridge International Computer Science 9618

tasks.title: School trip budget
tasks.question: Read a positive integer Students and a non-negative REAL TicketPrice. A coach costs 180.00 in total. Output the total trip cost and the cost per student, sharing the coach cost equally. You may assume the inputs have the stated types and ranges. Do not round the results.
tasks.hint: Add the coach charge once, before dividing by the number of students.
tasks.code:
DECLARE Students : INTEGER
DECLARE TicketPrice, TotalCost, CostEach : REAL
INPUT Students
INPUT TicketPrice
TotalCost ← Students * TicketPrice + 180.00
CostEach ← TotalCost / Students
OUTPUT TotalCost, CostEach
tasks.explanation: The multiplication accounts for every ticket. The fixed coach charge is then added to the total. Division produces a REAL result; Students cannot be zero under the question's precondition.
rubric: Ticket cost multiplied by student count
tasks.pitfall: Dividing only the ticket price by the number of students gives the wrong share of the total.

tasks.title: Parcel charge bands
tasks.question: Read a REAL Mass. If Mass is zero or negative, output Invalid mass. Otherwise charge 3.00 for a mass up to and including 1 kg, 5.50 for a mass above 1 kg and up to and including 5 kg, and 9.00 above 5 kg. Output only the applicable charge or the invalid message.
tasks.hint: Test the invalid range first, then put the remaining ranges in increasing order.
tasks.code:
DECLARE Mass : REAL
INPUT Mass
IF Mass <= 0 THEN
   OUTPUT "Invalid mass"
ELSE
   IF Mass <= 1 THEN
      OUTPUT 3.00
   ELSE
      IF Mass <= 5 THEN
         OUTPUT 5.50
      ELSE
         OUTPUT 9.00
      ENDIF
   ENDIF
ENDIF
tasks.explanation: Each ELSE removes a range already considered. By the time Mass <= 5 is tested, Mass is known to be greater than 1. The nested branches ensure exactly one output.
rubric: Read Mass with a suitable type
tasks.pitfall: Separate IF statements can print more than one price for the same mass.

tasks.title: Three chances to unlock
tasks.question: A practice lock accepts the STRING code 2468. Read at most three code attempts. Stop asking as soon as an attempt is correct. Output Access granted after a correct attempt, or Locked after three incorrect attempts. Treat the code as text; each INPUT supplies one attempt.
tasks.hint: Track both the number of attempts and whether the lock is open.
tasks.code:
DECLARE Attempt : STRING
DECLARE Attempts : INTEGER
DECLARE Unlocked : BOOLEAN
Attempts ← 0
Unlocked ← FALSE
WHILE (Attempts < 3) AND (Unlocked = FALSE)
   INPUT Attempt
   Attempts ← Attempts + 1
   IF Attempt = "2468" THEN
      Unlocked ← TRUE
   ENDIF
ENDWHILE
IF Unlocked THEN
   OUTPUT "Access granted"
ELSE
   OUTPUT "Locked"
ENDIF
tasks.explanation: The counter changes on every input, including a successful attempt. A successful third attempt is still accepted because the final message depends on Unlocked rather than the counter alone.
rubric: Input and counter update on each attempt
Compare with the correct STRING code
tasks.pitfall: Using Attempts = 3 to decide failure rejects a correct third attempt.

tasks.title: Temperature log
tasks.question: Read INTEGER temperatures until 999 is entered. The value 999 is a sentinel and must not be processed. Output the average of the readings, or No readings if the sentinel is the first input. Valid readings may be positive, zero, or negative. Assume every non-sentinel input is a valid temperature.
tasks.hint: Read once before the loop and again at its end. Protect the division when no readings exist.
tasks.code:
DECLARE Reading, Total, Count : INTEGER
DECLARE Average : REAL
Total ← 0
Count ← 0
INPUT Reading
WHILE Reading <> 999
   Total ← Total + Reading
   Count ← Count + 1
   INPUT Reading
ENDWHILE
IF Count = 0 THEN
   OUTPUT "No readings"
ELSE
   Average ← Total / Count
   OUTPUT Average
ENDIF
tasks.explanation: Testing the sentinel before accumulation excludes it from both Total and Count. The empty-data branch avoids division by zero. Negative readings require no special case.
rubric: Read the next value inside the loop
tasks.pitfall: Counting 999 as a reading changes both the numerator and the denominator.

tasks.title: Seats still available
tasks.question: Read eight INTEGER values into FreeSeats[1:8]. Each value is the number of free seats on one minibus and is guaranteed to be from 0 to 15 inclusive. Output how many minibuses have at least four free seats, and output the total number of free seats across all eight minibuses.
tasks.hint: A count of qualifying buses and a sum of seats measure different things.
tasks.code:
DECLARE FreeSeats : ARRAY[1:8] OF INTEGER
DECLARE Index, Suitable, Total : INTEGER
Suitable ← 0
Total ← 0
FOR Index ← 1 TO 8
   INPUT FreeSeats[Index]
   Total ← Total + FreeSeats[Index]
   IF FreeSeats[Index] >= 4 THEN
      Suitable ← Suitable + 1
   ENDIF
NEXT Index
OUTPUT Suitable, Total
tasks.explanation: Every input contributes its seat value to Total. Only inputs meeting the inclusive threshold contribute one to Suitable. All eight array positions are visited exactly once.
tasks.pitfall: Suitable must increase by one per qualifying bus, rather than by its seat count.

tasks.title: Mirror a message
tasks.question: Read a STRING Message, which may be empty. Build and output a second string containing the characters of Message in reverse order. Use LENGTH(S) for the number of characters and MID(S, Start, Count) for a substring; positions start at 1. Use & to concatenate strings. Do not call a built-in reverse function.
tasks.hint: Start with an empty result and visit the original positions from last to first.
tasks.code:
DECLARE Message, Mirrored : STRING
DECLARE Position : INTEGER
INPUT Message
Mirrored ← ""
FOR Position ← LENGTH(Message) TO 1 STEP -1
   Mirrored ← Mirrored & MID(Message, Position, 1)
NEXT Position
OUTPUT Mirrored
tasks.explanation: Each substring contains one character. For an empty input the starting position is zero, so the negative-step loop has no iterations and the result stays empty.
tasks.pitfall: Using + instead of & treats string joining like arithmetic.

tasks.title: Busiest activity row
tasks.question: Counts is an already populated INTEGER array with bounds [1:3,1:4]. Values are non-negative. Each row represents one activity and each column one session. Output each row total, then the row number with the largest total. If rows tie, choose the smallest row number. You do not need to read the array.
tasks.hint: Reset the row total inside the outer loop. A strict comparison preserves the first tied row.
tasks.code:
// Counts is supplied with bounds [1:3,1:4]
DECLARE Row, Column, RowTotal : INTEGER
DECLARE BestRow, BestTotal : INTEGER
BestRow ← 1
BestTotal ← -1
FOR Row ← 1 TO 3
   RowTotal ← 0
   FOR Column ← 1 TO 4
      RowTotal ← RowTotal + Counts[Row, Column]
   NEXT Column
   OUTPUT RowTotal
   IF RowTotal > BestTotal THEN
      BestTotal ← RowTotal
      BestRow ← Row
   ENDIF
NEXT Row
OUTPUT BestRow
tasks.explanation: Because all entries are non-negative, -1 is below every possible row total. Updating only for a strictly greater total keeps the earlier row in a tie.
rubric: Valid initial best row and total
Update total and row while preserving ties
tasks.pitfall: Resetting RowTotal before the outer loop produces running totals across rows.

tasks.title: First matching badge
tasks.question: Badges is an already populated STRING array with bounds [1:40]. N is an INTEGER from 0 to 40 giving the number of used entries. Read Target and output the index of its first occurrence within positions 1 to N, or 0 if it is absent. Repeated badge values are possible. Do not examine entries beyond N.
tasks.hint: Use position 0 for not found and stop the loop once it changes.
tests: Used badges A, C, A; Target A
Used badges A, C, A; Target Z
tasks.code:
// Badges and N are supplied
DECLARE Target : STRING
DECLARE Index, Position : INTEGER
INPUT Target
Index ← 1
Position ← 0
WHILE (Index <= N) AND (Position = 0)
   IF Badges[Index] = Target THEN
      Position ← Index
   ENDIF
   Index ← Index + 1
ENDWHILE
OUTPUT Position
tasks.explanation: The loop condition contains no array access. Consequently no assumption about short-circuit Boolean evaluation is needed to keep the array access safe. For N = 0, the body is skipped.
rubric: Read Target and initialise search state
Loop stops after the first match
Correct output for found and absent targets
tasks.pitfall: Continuing and overwriting Position on every match returns the last match.

tasks.title: Sort waiting times
tasks.question: Times is an already populated INTEGER array with bounds [1:30]. N, from 1 to 30, gives its used length. Sort the used entries into ascending order using bubble sort. End early if a whole pass makes no swaps. Output each used value after sorting. Duplicate values must be retained.
tasks.hint: After one full pass, the largest remaining value is already in its final position.
tasks.code:
// Times and N are supplied
DECLARE Last, Index, Temp : INTEGER
DECLARE Swapped : BOOLEAN
Last ← N
Swapped ← TRUE
WHILE (Last > 1) AND Swapped
   Swapped ← FALSE
   FOR Index ← 1 TO Last - 1
      IF Times[Index] > Times[Index + 1] THEN
         Temp ← Times[Index]
         Times[Index] ← Times[Index + 1]
         Times[Index + 1] ← Temp
         Swapped ← TRUE
      ENDIF
   NEXT Index
   Last ← Last - 1
ENDWHILE
FOR Index ← 1 TO N
   OUTPUT Times[Index]
NEXT Index
tasks.explanation: Each pass moves the largest unsorted value to Last. The next pass excludes that position. A pass without swaps proves that the remaining prefix is in order.
rubric: Shrink the bound and stop when sorted
tasks.pitfall: Comparing up to Last accesses Times[Last + 1], outside the active region.

tasks.title: Find a sorted catalogue code
tasks.question: Codes is an INTEGER array with bounds [1:100]. Its N used entries are already sorted in ascending order and contain distinct values; N is from 0 to 100. Read Target and use binary search to output its index, or 0 if absent. Do not sort the array or use linear search.
tasks.hint: Exclude the tested midpoint when narrowing the range.
tasks.code:
// Codes and N are supplied
DECLARE Target, Low, High, Mid, Position : INTEGER
INPUT Target
Low ← 1
High ← N
Position ← 0
WHILE (Low <= High) AND (Position = 0)
   Mid ← (Low + High) DIV 2
   IF Codes[Mid] = Target THEN
      Position ← Mid
   ELSE
      IF Codes[Mid] < Target THEN
         Low ← Mid + 1
      ELSE
         High ← Mid - 1
      ENDIF
   ENDIF
ENDWHILE
OUTPUT Position
tasks.explanation: Low and High describe an inclusive search interval. Removing Mid after a failed comparison guarantees progress. An empty array starts with Low > High and needs no special array access.
tasks.pitfall: Low ← Mid can repeat the same midpoint forever when the interval is small.

tasks.title: A reusable common-factor function
tasks.question: Write a function CommonFactor(A : INTEGER, B : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER that returns the greatest common divisor of two positive integers. Use this method: repeatedly replace A by B and B by the remainder of the old A divided by the old B, stopping when B becomes zero. Also show a call for 84 and 30 that outputs the return value.
tasks.hint: Save the remainder before overwriting either value.
tasks.code:
FUNCTION CommonFactor(A : INTEGER, B : INTEGER)
   RETURNS INTEGER
   DECLARE Remainder : INTEGER
   WHILE B <> 0
      Remainder ← A MOD B
      A ← B
      B ← Remainder
   ENDWHILE
   RETURN A
ENDFUNCTION

OUTPUT CommonFactor(84, 30)
tasks.explanation: The nonzero remainders decrease until B becomes zero. At that point A holds the greatest common divisor. The parameters are passed by value, so this function does not change the caller's variables.
rubric: Function header with typed parameters and return type
Loop stops when B is zero
Calculate A MOD B before overwriting
Replace B with the saved remainder
Correct output of a function call
tasks.pitfall: OUTPUT inside the function is not a substitute for returning a value to its caller.

tasks.title: Select the best project
tasks.question: Define a record type ProjectRecord with a STRING Title, an INTEGER Score, and a BOOLEAN Submitted. Projects is an already populated array of 20 such records; N, from 0 to 20, gives the used length. Output the title and score of the submitted project with the highest score, or No submissions. Scores are 0 to 100. On a tie, use the first project in array order.
tasks.hint: Track the winning index; index 0 can represent no eligible project.
tasks.code:
TYPE ProjectRecord
   DECLARE Title : STRING
   DECLARE Score : INTEGER
   DECLARE Submitted : BOOLEAN
ENDTYPE
// Supplied: Projects : ARRAY[1:20] OF ProjectRecord
// Supplied: N : INTEGER
DECLARE Index, BestIndex, BestScore : INTEGER
BestIndex ← 0
BestScore ← -1
FOR Index ← 1 TO N
   IF Projects[Index].Submitted THEN
      IF Projects[Index].Score > BestScore THEN
         BestScore ← Projects[Index].Score
         BestIndex ← Index
      ENDIF
   ENDIF
NEXT Index
IF BestIndex = 0 THEN
   OUTPUT "No submissions"
ELSE
   OUTPUT Projects[BestIndex].Title,
          Projects[BestIndex].Score
ENDIF
tasks.explanation: BestScore = -1 is safe because valid scores are non-negative. The best index remains zero when no submitted project is visited. Strictly greater comparison preserves the first eligible project on a tie.
rubric: Record type with all three fields and types
Visit only the N used records
tasks.pitfall: Selecting the largest score before checking Submitted can choose an ineligible project.

advanced.title: Recursive digit total
advanced.question: Write a recursive function DigitTotal(N : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER for N >= 0. It must return the sum of the decimal digits of N, without strings or loops. Use a base case for N < 10. Trace the calls and returned values for DigitTotal(5072). Explain why recursion terminates.
advanced.scaffold: Use N MOD 10 for the last digit and N DIV 10 for the remaining digits.
advanced.code:
FUNCTION DigitTotal(N : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
   IF N < 10 THEN
      RETURN N
   ELSE
      RETURN (N MOD 10) + DigitTotal(N DIV 10)
   ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
advanced.explanation: Calls descend through 5072, 507, 50, and 5. The base call returns 5. Unwinding gives 0 + 5 = 5, then 7 + 5 = 12, then 2 + 12 = 14. For each recursive call with N >= 10, integer division by 10 produces a smaller non-negative integer; it eventually reaches a single digit.
rubric: Correct call and return trace for 5072
Termination explained using a decreasing input
advanced.pitfall: Calling DigitTotal(N) again leaves the argument unchanged and never reaches the base case.

advanced.title: Safe stack removal
advanced.question: Stack is a global ARRAY[1:6] OF INTEGER and Top is a global INTEGER. Top = 0 means empty; otherwise Stack[Top] is the top item. Write Pop(BYREF Item : INTEGER, BYREF Success : BOOLEAN) as a procedure. If empty, set Success to FALSE and leave Item and Top unchanged. Otherwise copy the top item to Item, decrease Top, and set Success to TRUE. Show two calls when Top = 1 and Stack[1] = 42.
advanced.scaffold: Use the precondition 0 <= Top <= 6. Only access Stack[Top] after ruling out an empty stack.
advanced.code:
PROCEDURE Pop(BYREF Item : INTEGER,
              BYREF Success : BOOLEAN)
   IF Top = 0 THEN
      Success ← FALSE
   ELSE
      Item ← Stack[Top]
      Top ← Top - 1
      Success ← TRUE
   ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE

DECLARE Value : INTEGER
DECLARE OK : BOOLEAN
CALL Pop(Value, OK)
OUTPUT Value, OK
CALL Pop(Value, OK)
OUTPUT Value, OK
advanced.explanation: Starting from the specified state, the first call outputs 42, TRUE and leaves Top = 0. The second outputs 42, FALSE and leaves Top = 0. Value retains its earlier value after the failed call. BYREF allows Item and Success to update the variables passed by the caller. Global Stack and Top are supplied state, so no local redeclarations are needed.
rubric: Preserve Item and Top on empty
Correct state and outputs for both calls
advanced.pitfall: Decreasing Top before reading the item removes the wrong element and can access index 0.

advanced.title: Circular queue insertion
advanced.question: Queue is a global ARRAY[1:5] OF STRING. Global INTEGERs Front, Rear, and Count describe it: Front is the next item to remove, Rear is the next free slot to fill, and Count is the number stored. Initially Front = 1, Rear = 1, Count = 0. Write Enqueue(Value : STRING, BYREF Success : BOOLEAN). If full, report failure and change no queue state. Otherwise store Value, advance Rear with wraparound, increase Count, and report success. Enqueue must not change Front.
advanced.scaffold: For a wraparound trace, begin at Front = 4, Rear = 5, Count = 1 with Queue[4] = "old". Insert "new" and state the resulting pointers, count, and slot contents.
advanced.code:
PROCEDURE Enqueue(Value : STRING,
                  BYREF Success : BOOLEAN)
   IF Count = 5 THEN
      Success ← FALSE
   ELSE
      Queue[Rear] ← Value
      Rear ← Rear + 1
      IF Rear > 5 THEN
         Rear ← 1
      ENDIF
      Count ← Count + 1
      Success ← TRUE
   ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE
advanced.explanation: Rear always identifies the next insertion slot. With Front = 4, Rear = 5 and Count = 1, insertion writes new to Queue[5], wraps Rear to 1, and makes Count = 2. Front stays 4 and Queue[4] stays old. With Count = 5 the failure branch performs no writes to Queue, Front, Rear, or Count.
rubric: Failure status without changing queue state
advanced.pitfall: Front = Rear can describe either empty or full here; Count distinguishes those states.

advanced.title: Build a reference-only file
advanced.question: The existing text file resources.txt contains one resource code per line. Copy every line beginning with the exact uppercase prefix REF- into a new text file reference.txt, in the same order. Ignore shorter and non-matching lines. Output the number copied. Handle an empty source file. You may assume file operations succeed. LENGTH(S) gives the length and MID(S, Start, Count) gives a substring from position 1.
advanced.scaffold: Check that a line has at least four characters before taking its four-character prefix. Opening reference.txt in WRITE mode replaces any existing contents.
advanced.code:
DECLARE Line : STRING
DECLARE Copied : INTEGER
Copied ← 0
OPENFILE "resources.txt" FOR READ
OPENFILE "reference.txt" FOR WRITE
WHILE NOT EOF("resources.txt")
   READFILE "resources.txt", Line
   IF LENGTH(Line) >= 4 THEN
      IF MID(Line, 1, 4) = "REF-" THEN
         WRITEFILE "reference.txt", Line
         Copied ← Copied + 1
      ENDIF
   ENDIF
ENDWHILE
CLOSEFILE "resources.txt"
CLOSEFILE "reference.txt"
OUTPUT Copied
advanced.explanation: EOF is checked before each read, including the first one, so an empty input produces an empty output file and a count of zero. The nested length check keeps the substring call valid without depending on short-circuit evaluation. Writing immediately preserves the source order.
rubric: Open input for READ and output for WRITE
Initialise count and use STRING line storage
Guard substring with a length check
Output count, including zero for empty input
advanced.pitfall: APPEND mode retains old output, so rerunning the program would duplicate earlier results.
